decision: Should 'How we're different' stay a comparison table, or show the difference another way?
where: Live prototype on the home page: /?variant=now|A|B|C|D|E (component src/components/compare-prototype.tsx, branch site/compare-prototype). Screenshots: <key>-1440.png and <key>-375.png.
invariants: same facts as the live table (.design/research/competitors-2026-10.md); categories only, no competitor names
same headline and eyebrow, except C, which replaces the headline with the comparison sentence
warm look tokens (D-034) and the featured-plan grain wash (D-037)
same slot on the page: after Our promise, before Pricing
assumption_to_check: B and E turn the tutor's hourly rate into a month at one hour a week (4 x $40-$100 = $160-$400). The live table does not state this number.

options.cost: 20 sentences, no verdict, price row buried

options.bet: Make the headline into three panels: tutor, learning centre, us, one price each
options.benefit: Price leads; reads in 5 seconds; each panel says what you get
options.cost: Drops the row-by-row detail; apps become a footnote
options.risk: Looks like a second pricing section right before Pricing

options.bet: Show monthly cost as range bars on one scale
options.benefit: The shortest bar is the argument; no reading needed
options.cost: Only cost; apps show as cheaper than us
options.risk: Relies on the $160-$400 tutor month assumption; 'priced like neither' lands, 'personal' does not

options.bet: No table: one sentence with the three prices, small enough to sit under 'Why choose'
options.cost: No detail on adapting, gaps or paper
options.risk: Too thin to answer 'why not a tutor?'

options.bet: Keep the table, but every cell is a verdict glyph and two or three words; our column outlined top to bottom
options.benefit: Scannable by glyph; keeps all four rows of detail
options.cost: Still a grid; still four columns
options.risk: Tutor shows many full checks, so the difference reads as cost only

options.bet: A month, as three receipts: tutor, us, learning centre
options.benefit: Parent language (what the money buys); our receipt lists five included items; tactile, fits the paper idea
options.risk: Relies on the $160-$400 tutor month assumption; receipt metaphor may read as a gimmick
